newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb knocks goods train off track in India.
newsitem.headline: Bomb knocks goods train off track in India.

text.p: A bomb blew a goods train off the track in India's Jammu and Kashmir state, minutes before a crowded passenger train was scheduled to pass by, a senior police officer said on Tuesday.

Deputy inspector-general of police S.K. Mishra told Reuters in the state's winter capital Jammu that the device, packed with powerful Research Developed Explosive (RDX), exploded late on Monday near Raya Morh, 18 km (11 miles) southwest of Jammu.
The blast knocked seven carriages of the goods train off the track. No one was injured, Mishra said.
Railway officials said a packed express passenger train was following the goods train but was halted five km (three miles) from the site of the blast.
Mishra said no one had claimed responsibility for the blast.

The explosion ripped up four metres (12 feet) of track and forced the suspension of rail traffic between Punjab state and Jammu and Kashmir, stranding thousands of travellers, officials said. Rail traffic was expected to resume on Tuesday.
The blast occurred one day after one kg (2.2 lb) of RDX was found on a Jammu-bound passenger bus near Kathua, 80 km (50 miles) south of Jammu.
Last Friday, a bomb planted by suspected separatist militants exploded on a bus in Pathankot town, about 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Jammu, killing seven passengers.
Jammu and Kashmir state, which borders Pakistan, has been racked by seven years of separatist insurgency in which more than 20,000 people have died.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training guerrillas fighting New Delhi's rule over the mostly Moslem Kashmir Valley. Islamabad says it provides only moral and diplomatic support.
